updates.title: Federal NFA Ruling: Important Limits for New Jersey Owners
updates.summary:
A significant federal firearms ruling remains in place after the U.S. Department of Justice decided not to appeal.

On August 5, 2026, a federal court in Texas ruled that certain National Firearms Act registration and approval requirements exceeded Congress’s taxing authority after federal making and transfer taxes were eliminated for the affected firearms.

The consolidated cases—Silencer Shop Foundation v. ATF and the NRA-supported Jensen v. ATF—address suppressors, short-barreled rifles, short-barreled shotguns, and certain other NFA firearms. Coverage differs between the plaintiff groups: “any other weapons” (AOWs) are covered for the Silencer Shop Foundation parties, but not the Jensen parties.

The protections are limited. The injunction covers the plaintiffs and, where applicable, their members, customers, agencies, and political subdivisions, including current and future members and customers as applicable. It does not repeal the entire NFA or eliminate other applicable federal requirements. Federal restrictions on certain dealer transfers and interstate transportation of short-barreled rifles and shotguns remain applicable; machine guns and destructive devices are not covered.

For New Jersey owners: This federal ruling does not overturn New Jersey’s separate firearms laws. Suppressors and firearms meeting New Jersey’s “sawed-off shotgun” definition remain generally prohibited for civilian possession, subject to specific statutory exceptions. The ruling does not expand New Jersey carry privileges or change restricted-place rules.

DOJ’s October 1 filing confirmed its decision not to appeal, referencing a September 24 letter to Congress, and stated that ATF was finalizing public guidance. As of October 8, 2026, no later material ruling or public ATF guidance resolving the injunction’s scope was identified in the sources checked. Further clarification remains pending.

The NRA’s October 8 email highlights an Armed Citizen podcast discussion between Frank Miniter and Josh Savani about the decision. The podcast is additional commentary; the court documents and applicable statutes govern.

Do not treat this ruling as blanket permission to purchase, make, possess, or transport an affected firearm. Confirm current federal and New Jersey requirements with a qualified New Jersey firearms attorney.

CarryAware provides educational information, not legal advice.

updates.title: Point Pleasant Moves to Refund Municipal Carry-Permit Fee
updates.summary:
Point Pleasant Borough has taken a step toward providing relief from the municipal portion of New Jersey’s permit-to-carry application fee.

The Borough Council’s September 21 agenda included authorization to refund the municipal portion of the fee imposed under N.J.S.A. 2C:58-4. Adoption has not yet been independently verified.

Applicants may still be required to pay the fee first and request reimbursement afterward. Eligibility dates, documentation requirements, and refund procedures are determined locally. Confirm the current process with Point Pleasant Borough before applying.

View CarryAwareNJ’s Municipal Carry-Fee Tracker for the statewide directory, policy research status, known refund amounts, effective dates, and sources. Listing a municipality does not mean its policy has been verified.

Community credit: Teacher in NJ (@teacher_in_nj) and Jay Costa (@jaycostausa).

CarryAwareNJ provides informational updates only and does not provide legal advice.

updates.title: Federal Handgun Sales Update: Ages 18–20
updates.summary: On September 18, 2026, the U.S. Department of Justice announced that its Office of Legal Counsel concluded the federal restriction preventing federally licensed dealers from selling handguns to otherwise-lawful adults ages 18–20 is unconstitutional and cannot be criminally enforced. This is a DOJ legal opinion—not a U.S. Supreme Court ruling—and it does not override state law. As of September 19, updated public ATF dealer guidance was not yet available. New Jersey law remains unchanged: N.J.S.A. 2C:58-3(c)(4) prohibits issuing a permit to purchase a handgun to anyone under 21. Continue following all current New Jersey requirements and applicable dealer guidance.
updates.status: DOJ Opinion; New Jersey Law Unchanged
updates.sourceTitle: U.S. Department of Justice — Handgun Sales to Adults Ages 18–20

updates.title: Gun For Hire Team Steps Up Aboard Flight 618
updates.summary: Rich and Juan from Gun For Hire helped the crew and fellow passengers restrain an allegedly violent passenger aboard American Airlines Flight 618 from Dallas-Fort Worth to Newark on September 3. The flight diverted to Baltimore, where law enforcement took over. Gun For Hire has collected the interviews, video, and national coverage.

updates.title: NJ Assault-Firearm and Magazine Ruling Stayed
updates.summary: The en banc Third Circuit previously held New Jersey's bans on commonly owned semiautomatic rifles and magazines capable of holding more than 10 rounds unconstitutional. On August 4, 2026, the court granted New Jersey a stay while the State seeks U.S. Supreme Court review. While the stay remains in effect, New Jersey's current assault-firearm restrictions and 10-round magazine limit remain enforceable.
updates.sourceTitle: NRA-ILA — Third Circuit Grants Stay in AWB/Mag Ban Case

updates.title: NJ Carry Restrictions Await En Banc Third Circuit Ruling
updates.summary: The full Third Circuit is reconsidering challenges to New Jersey's post-Bruen carry restrictions, including numerous designated sensitive places and related carry provisions. En banc oral argument was held on February 11, 2026. After the U.S. Supreme Court's Wolford decision, the parties filed supplemental briefs on July 8, 2026. The en banc Third Circuit decision remains pending.
